Agent Protocols, Traced

One agent purchase, “reorder printer ink under $60”, followed message by message across six parties. Each arrow is coloured by the protocol that carries it: MCP for tools, A2A between agents, ACP or UCP for checkout, AP2 for signed consent, card rails or x402 for the money. Press play, change the switches, or tap an arrow.

Tap an arrow

Each arrow is one message. The panel shows which protocol carries it, a shortened example and what the receiver checks.

Our worked example, built from the published specifications (MCP 2026-07-28, A2A 1.0, ACP 2026-04-17, AP2 v0.2, x402). Messages are shortened and not executed; few real systems use all of these protocols at once. Read the series: Part 1 map · MCP · A2A · payments.

Disclosure: Claude, made by Anthropic, helps write this site. MCP was introduced by Anthropic; A2A, AP2 and UCP started at Google, an investor in Anthropic; ACP is maintained by OpenAI, an Anthropic competitor, and Stripe.
